Comparative Timelines

The World's Four Largest Religions

Roughly 5.8 billion people — about seven in ten humans alive — identify with one of these four traditions. Each timeline below runs vertically from origins to the present, with a separate view mapping how each tradition split into its branches.

This is a historical reference, not a devotional one. It describes what each tradition teaches without endorsing or disputing it, and it records the documented historical record in full — including conquest, forced conversion, persecution of outsiders and of internal dissenters, religious warfare, and institutional abuse. Every tradition here has been both persecutor and persecuted. Where scholars disagree on dates, origins, adherent counts, or death tolls, the entry says so.

Branch Trees

Skip the timelines and go straight to the family trees — every denomination, sect, school and order of all four traditions, drawn as branching diagrams. Click any branch for its history and size.
